speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CSF and MRI effectively rule out meningitis or encephalitis, while the massively elevated CK of 5600 U/L strongly points to rhabdomyolysis as the cause of your altered mental status. This combination of fever, confusion, and muscle breakdown is highly suggestive of a severe rickettsial infection, such as RMSF or a severe viral myositis like Influenza B. Do you recall any recent exposure to ticks, rodents, or a rash that appeared on your palms or soles? REQUEST TEST: Anti-Rickettsia serology, Viral PCR panel.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Influenza B-associated severe myositis with rhabdomyolysis. The negative viral PCR in the previous round may be due to the timing of the test (viral load may have cleared) or a specific strain not covered; the clinical picture of high fever, altered mental status, and massive CK elevation without CNS involvement is classic for this condition. I recommend immediate aggressive IV fluid resuscitation and monitoring for acute kidney injury.
